text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: autoscaler-lag detected for service= inference-queue-proxy - queue_length=9850 (> threshold=5000), avg_processing_ms=1200, target_replicas=12, current_replicas=6. PagerDuty: PD-INC-8912 paged primary oncall. https://metrics.redwood.internal/d/inference/queue?from=now-15m
Priya Sharma: acked. I'm on it. pulling up dashboards now.
Sam Kim: ack. grabbing runbook link and will attempt manual scale while we investigate.
Priya Sharma: notes from grafana - sustained enqueue rate spike from a small set of customers (~10k rps) starting 00:12 UTC, sustained 18m. autoscaler target didn't increase beyond 12 due to CPU-based policy; CPU per-pod < 60% because tasks are IO-bound -> autoscaler didn't trigger.
Sam Kim: ugh, right. autoscaler is CPU-based. runbook suggests manual replica bump or switch to custom HPA metric (queue_length). Trying manual scale to 24 replicas now: `kubectl scale deployment inference-queue-proxy --replicas=24 -n prod`
oncall-runbook-bot: Runbook step: when queue backlog > 5000 and autoscaler hasn't scaled, increase replicas or apply burst_policy. See https://runbooks.redwood/internal/queue-backlog.
Mike Alvarez: I see scaling in kube events, but pods are Pending (insufficient capacity in us-west-2). autoscaler wouldn't help if cloud capacity is the limiter.
Priya Sharma: can we allow burst to other region? route to us-west-1 secondary pool?
Jordan Lee: routing change possible. I'll flip route for non-SLA traffic to secondary region (us-west-1), leave vip pinned for enterprise. Doing a staged reroute: adjust weight 70->30 via traffic-router console.
Sam Kim: command to move non-SLA lane: `curl -X POST https://router.redwood.internal/route -d '{"service":"inference","lane":"non-sla","weights":{"us-west-2":30,"us-west-1":70}}'` (placeholder)
Priya Sharma: doing that—will monitor queue size.
pagerduty-bot: PD-INC-8912 status: acknowledged by Priya Sharma at 00:35 UTC. Escalation timer paused.
Priya Sharma: early indicators: queue length dropping from 9850 -> 6400 after manual partial reroute, avg_processing_ms still high (~1100ms).
Mike Alvarez: cloud capacity request in flight to increase instance pool in us-west-2 (submitted ticket CLOUD-4578). ETA ~15-20m.
Jordan Lee: reroute completed, non-SLA traffic is now 70% us-west-1. Observability: us-west-1 pools healthy, CPU on new pods ~30%, latency ~450ms, queue drain rate improved.
Sam Kim: adding temporary autoscaler override: switching HPA to queue_length metric. `kubectl apply -f hpa-override.yaml` snippet: ```apiVersion: autoscaling/v2beta2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: inference-queue-proxy-queue-hpa
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: inference-queue-proxy
  metrics:
  - type: Object
    object:
      describedObject:
        kind: Service
        name: inference-queue
      metric:
        name: queue_length
      target:
        type: Value
        value: "5000"```
Priya Sharma: applying override now. will watch for rapid scale and any side effects.
oncall-runbook-bot: Note: HPA override is temporary. Revert after incident resolution.
Priya Sharma: HPA override applied, Kubernetes events show scale-up to 30 replicas requested. Some pods still in Pending but overall ready pods increased to 20. queue now 6400 -> 4200 in 6m.
Sam Kim: good. customers seeing errors? support dashboard shows error rate for generation API up from 0.2% -> 1.8% for non-enterprise customers. Enterprise tier unaffected.
Priya Sharma: posted a brief internal incident update to #incidents and customer-impact doc. cc @support.
Mike Alvarez: cloud pool scaled, pending pod backlog cleared. new pods stable.
Jordan Lee: after reroute and HPA override, throughput normalized. queue length now 1200 and trending down.
Priya Sharma: plan: keep HPA override for 30m, then revert to CPU-based policy and open follow-up to change autoscaler to use queue_length for inference-queue-proxy. Creating follow-up ticket OPS-1092.
Sam Kim: thumbs: :thumbsup: will add thermal-test to prevent regressions.
Priya Sharma: handoff to next oncall at 01:00 UTC — @Sam you'll monitor for the next 45m?
Sam Kim: yep i'll watch alerts, replay runbook if it surfaces.
pagerduty-bot: PD-INC-8912 status: resolved at 01:05 UTC (automated) - manual close after metrics stable.
Priya Sharma: closing thread with brief timeline: 00:12 spike -> 00:28 initial PD page -> 00:35 manual reroute + manual scale -> 00:47 HPA override -> 01:05 normalized. Impact: degraded latency and elevated error rate for non-enterprise customers for ~50m. Follow-ups: OPS-1092 (HPA metric change), CLOUD-4578 capacity review, TEST-223 add chaos test for sudden enqueue spikes.
Sam Kim: thanks team. :heart:
